models.name: discussion_board_configs
models.description:
System-wide configuration key-value stores.

This table stores all system configuration parameters as key-value pairs.
Each configuration key appears exactly once, allowing for easy reading and update of settings.

The value is stored as a string to accommodate various configuration types (boolean, numeric, string) that will be parsed by the application.
Configuration updates trigger timestamps for tracking changes.
Soft deletion is supported to maintain historical configuration states without removing records from the database.

Key configuration features include:
- Feature flags for enabling/disabling platform features
- Performance parameters such as rate limits and timeouts
- Global settings affecting user experience

plainFields.name: key
plainFields.description: Configuration parameter name, must be unique across all configurations.

plainFields.name: value
plainFields.description: Configuration parameter value, stored as a string representing the actual value (e.g., 'true' for boolean, '50' for integer). The application parses this value to the appropriate type.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the configuration was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the configuration was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the configuration was soft-deleted (null means active).

models.name: discussion_board_channels
models.description:
Channel configuration entities for organizing discussion content.

Stores named channels with branding and content rules to structure discussions into thematic topics. Each channel has unique branding for visual differentiation in the UI.

Channels are foundational to the forum's structure and cannot be deleted from the system (only hidden for moderation). Business rules dictate that a channel must have a unique name, description, and branding.

Channel rules define required content formatting, post types, and behavior guidelines to maintain topic focus and quality across the discussion platform.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Channel name displayed to users. Must be unique across all channels.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of the channel's purpose and scope for users.

plainFields.name: branding_color
plainFields.description: Hex color code used for branding. Example: #3498db.

plainFields.name: content_rules
plainFields.description: Text rules for content posted in this channel. Includes formatting requirements and topic restrictions.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Time when the channel was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Time when the channel was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Time when the channel was soft-deleted. Null if active.

models.name: discussion_board_members
models.description:
Core member account details for authenticated users.

Stores authentication credentials, basic profile information, and membership status for registered members.

Each member has a unique email address for login and profile management. Account status tracks validity (active, suspended, banned), supporting moderation workflows.

Email is required for login and must be unique. Password is securely hashed, and temporal fields track creation/modification with soft delete capability for data integrity.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: User's display name for public profiles, may be left blank.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Member's email address used for authentication. Must be unique across all members.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Securely hashed password for authentication. Never stored in plain text.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current membership status indicating account validity (active, suspended, banned).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when member account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last account modification.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of soft deletion to preserve audit trails.

models.name: discussion_board_admins
models.description:
Administrative accounts with elevated system privileges and moderation capabilities.

Stores accounts for system administrators who can manage user content, configure system settings, and perform moderation actions. Each admin account includes authentication credentials, access level configuration, and system role details.

Admins have distinct capabilities compared to regular members, with permissions for full system access and moderation workflows.
Scenario: An admin account created by superadmin for system management requires secure password storage and predefined access levels.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Admin email address used for authentication and account recovery. Must be unique across all administrative accounts.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Password hash storing the admin's authentication credentials. Does not store plaintext passwords for security reasons.

plainFields.name: system_access_level
plainFields.description: Administrative access level representing the privileges granted to this account. Valid values: 'superadmin', 'full-access', 'moderation-only'.

plainFields.name: moderation_capabilities
plainFields.description: Indicates if the admin account has moderation capabilities. True for admins who can review and manage content.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the admin account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the admin account was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the admin account was marked for deletion (soft delete).

models.name: discussion_board_member_sessions
models.description:
Tracks active login sessions for members, including expiration timestamps and device information.

Records session details for authenticated members to enable secure session management and activity tracking. Each session links to a specific member through the primary account.

Supports session duration tracking, device identification (IP address), and connection context (URLs and referrers) necessary for security monitoring and user activity audits.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address associated with the session connection.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Full URL used for the connection.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: URL that referred to the current connection.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of session creation.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when session expires (nullable if session is ongoing).

models.name: discussion_board_admin_sessions
models.description:
Tracks active admin login sessions with connection details for audit and activity tracking.

Maintains session connection context including client IP, URL, and referrer information. Session data is managed through admin identity flows rather than standalone operations.

Includes session creation and expiration timestamps for activity monitoring and session management.

Required fields follow exact session table specification without additional metadata. Composite index on [admin_id, created_at] ensures efficient query patterns for activity streams.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address of client connecting to system.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Connection URL for session tracking.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL from which session was initiated.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Session creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Session expiration timestamp.

models.name: discussion_board_articles
models.description:
Core table storing article content and moderation workflow states.

Articles represent user-generated content in the discussion board. Each article is authored by a member, contains a title, content body, and follows a moderation workflow from submission to publication.

Article content remains intact even if the author is deleted or changes their status, ensuring historical record integrity. Moderation status tracks the article's progression through review queues and final publication state.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Article title reflecting core content.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: Main article content body with markdown support.

plainFields.name: moderation_status
plainFields.description: Current status in moderation workflow. Valid values: pending, approved, rejected.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Article creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last modification timestamp.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Deletion timestamp for soft delete implementation.

models.name: discussion_board_article_images
models.description:
Stores uploaded images associated with discussion board articles. Contains file metadata, dimensions for display purposes, and automatic resizing parameters for optimized content delivery.

Each image record is created when media is uploaded to an article. Images can be deleted independently but remain linked to their parent article for historical consistency. The table supports batch image uploads and individual image management through the article's media interface.

All image metadata is stored at original resolution to enable consistent scaling across different display contexts. The table design allows for efficient filtering by article ID and upload timestamp.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Article this image belongs to. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}

plainFields.name: url
plainFields.description: Full URL path to the image file in storage.

plainFields.name: width
plainFields.description: Image width in pixels at original resolution.

plainFields.name: height
plainFields.description: Image height in pixels at original resolution.

plainFields.name: mime_type
plainFields.description: MIME type of the image file (e.g., image/jpeg).

plainFields.name: size
plainFields.description: File size in bytes.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when image was uploaded.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when image metadata was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when image was soft-deleted (null if active).

models.name: discussion_board_article_files
models.description:
Stores uploaded files attached to articles with type, size, and display information for PDF, DOCX, and XLSX formats.

Maintains complete metadata for all file attachments across articles, including file type constraints and display preferences. Each file attachment is uniquely associated with a specific article through the system's reference structure. Supports soft deletion for content moderation while preserving historical attachment records. File size and type validations enforce platform-wide attachment rules established in the Attachment component.

Independent file listing and filtering capabilities allow users to access all attachments across articles regardless of their parent article context. The attachment metadata enables sorting and filtering based on file type and size, supporting use cases across different content types.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Article this file belongs to. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

plainFields.name: file_type
plainFields.description: MIME type identifier for the file. Valid values: application/pdf, application/vnd.ms-excel, application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document.

plainFields.name: file_size
plainFields.description: File size in bytes. Follows platform size limits of maximum 50MB.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: User-visible name for the file. Used in UI for attachment listings and downloads.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of when the file was attached to the article.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last modification to attachment metadata.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when attachment was soft-deleted. Null indicates active attachment.

models.name: discussion_board_attachment_images
models.description:
Stores uploaded discussion board images along with their resolution and metadata for display purposes.

Each image attachment is independently managed but linked to a specific article through its foreign key reference. The resolution data (width, height) and file size support client-side display optimization and validation logic for image upload requirements. Soft deletion is supported via the deleted_at timestamp to maintain audit trails of image usage without permanently removing data.

plainFields.name: filename
plainFields.description: Original file name of the uploaded image.

plainFields.name: mime_type
plainFields.description: MIME type of the image (e.g., image/jpeg).

plainFields.name: width
plainFields.description: Width of the image in pixels.

plainFields.name: height
plainFields.description: Height of the image in pixels.

plainFields.name: file_size
plainFields.description: Size of the file in bytes.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the attachment was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the attachment was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the attachment was soft-deleted (if applicable).

models.name: discussion_board_attachment_files
models.description:
Stores file attachments with MIME type validation, size limits, and display information for PDF, DOCX, and XLSX formats.

This table manages all file attachments in the discussion board platform that are not restricted to specific content types. It captures essential metadata for user-facing file operations including download, preview, and display.

File attachments can be linked to discussion articles through a foreign key relationship. Each attachment record maintains its own metadata regardless of which article it's associated with, supporting features like global file search and independent file management.

The system validates file types to ensure PDF, DOCX, and XLSX formats are allowed in the standard library, making this table compatible with file processing workflows.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Article attachment's lifetime is tied to the parent article. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

plainFields.name: filename
plainFields.description: Actual filename of the attached file stored on the server.

plainFields.name: mime_type
plainFields.description: MIME type of the document including format specification (application/pdf, application/vnd.ms-excel).

plainFields.name: file_size
plainFields.description: File size in bytes. Enforces size limits for different document types.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: The name shown to users when displaying the file to them.

plainFields.name: original_filename
plainFields.description: Original filename as provided by the user during upload.

plainFields.name: stored_path
plainFields.description: Server path where the file is permanently stored.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the attachment was first uploaded to the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the attachment metadata was last modified, not including content updates.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the attachment was soft-deleted, or null indicating it's still active.

models.name: discussion_board_moderation_queue
models.description:
Tracks articles that require moderator review before being published, with article submission status and initial submission time.

This table manages all articles awaiting content moderation. Each entry represents an article submission requiring verification before publication. The status field tracks moderation progress (pending, approved, rejected).

Articles remain associated with their original content even after moderation, preserving historical workflow context. Moderators can view the submission time, original article details, and reason for rejection if applicable.

The foreign key to articles ensures historical linkage while allowing article content updates without affecting moderation history.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_articles_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the article being moderated {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_members_id
foreignFields.description: Creator member who submitted the article {@link discussion_board_members.id}.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current moderation status. Valid values: pending, approved, rejected. Status transitions follow moderation workflow rules.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Reason for rejection (if applicable). Used by moderators to communicate rejection rationale to submitters.

plainFields.name: submitted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the article was submitted for moderation. Used for queue prioritization and workflow tracking.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Entry creation timestamp for the moderation queue record.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for the queue record.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp for record management without data loss.

models.name: discussion_board_moderation_actions
models.description:
Records all moderator actions on articles including approvals, rejections with required reasons, and timestamps for all moderation activities.

Stores each moderation action with its status (approved, rejected, pending), rejection reason (when applicable), and timestamps. Each action references an article in the Discussion Articles component for context. Supports audit trails and historical analysis through complete recording of all moderation decisions, including reasons for rejections.

The reason field is required when the status is 'rejected' but optional for other statuses. Soft deletion capabilities allow for content recovery without data loss.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: The article that was moderated. {@link discussion_board_articles.id.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Moderation action status. Valid values: approved, rejected, pending.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Reason for rejection. Required when status is 'rejected'. Optional for other statuses.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the moderation action was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the moderation action was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the moderation action was soft-deleted. Null indicates active status.
